Though these matters are listed for Admission, with the consent of the learned counsel for the parties, the same are taken up for final disposal.

2. These two appeals are directed against the judgment and award, dated 01.06.2017, passed in M.V.C. No.5/2016 by the IX Additional District and Sessions Judge and Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi (for short, 'the Tribunal') and praying for enhancement of compensation.

entities.text: Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The claimants are in appeal in M.F.A. No.103368/2017 dis-satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal and praying for enhancement of compensation, whereas the insurance company is in appeal in M.F.A. No.103089/2017 questioning the liability and praying to set aside the liability saddled on it.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties herein would be referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal.

Brief facts of the case leading to filing of this appeal are that,
(a) The claimants - parents and sister of one Gadigeppa, who died in a road traffic accident, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation.

It is stated that, on 30.07.2015, when the deceased was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-22/EN-0706, a KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-42/F-654 came at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the motor cycle which resulted in the death of said Gadigeppa.

It is stated that the deceased was aged 25 years as on the date of the accident, and he was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/- per month by doing private service and Rs.10,000/- from the milk vending business.
(b) On issuance of notice, the respondent-North West Karnataka Road Transport Corporation (for short, NC: 2024:KHC-D:7821-DB 'the Corporation') appeared and filed its objections denying the averments made in the claim petition and contended that the accident had occurred due to rash and The Divisional Manager vs Smt. Jayashree W/O Fakirappa Jaragu on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183125908/
4 negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased himself.
Further, it is contended that the claim is exorbitant and excessive.
Thus, it prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
(c) Before the Tribunal, the mother of the deceased was examined as P.W.1 apart from marking six documents as Exs.P1 to P6.
No witness was examined nor was any document produced on behalf of the respondent.

(d) Based on the material on record, the Tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.6,42,000/-
with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit of compensation amount.

While awarding the above compensation, the Tribunal assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month, adopted NC: 2024:KHC-D:7821-DB multiplier '18', and deducted 50% of the assessed income towards personal expenses of the deceased.

The Tribunal apportioned the contributory negligence on part of the driver of bus and deceased in the ratio of 75:25.
5.
Heard learned counsel Smt. Shruti A.Neelopant for Sri. Shriharsh A.Neelopant, for the appellants/claimants, and learned Counsel Sri. S.L.Matti for the respondent-Corporation.
Perused the appeal papers as well as the records of the Tribunal.
6. Learned counsel for the appellants/claimants would submit that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- by doing private service and Rs.10,000/- from milk vending business.

She would further submit that the Tribunal, without appreciating the evidence of P.W.1, assessed the income at Rs.7,000/- per month and thus, the Tribunal committed a grave error in assessing the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month.

Further, learned counsel would submit that the Tribunal failed to NC: 2024:KHC-D:7821-DB award compensation towards 'future prospects' which the claimants would be entitled at the rate of 40% of assessed income since the deceased was aged 25 years as on the date of the accident.

7. The learned counsel for the appellants/claimants would submit that the Tribunal committed grave error in saddling 25% of the negligence on the deceased only on the ground that the deceased rider of the motorcycle had no valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.

Learned counsel would submit that, mere non-possession of driving licence cannot be a reason to attribute negligence on the part of the deceased and, in that regard, she places reliance on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Dinesh Kumar J. Alias Dinesh J. Vs.

. Thus, she prayed to allow the appeal.
Per contra, Sri. S.L.Matti, learned counsel for the respondent-Corporation would submit that the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper.
Learned counsel would submit that, in the absence of any material to establish the income, the notional income assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.7,000/- per month is proper and correct.

Further, learned counsel would submit that, the Tribunal has rightly saddled 25% of contributory negligence on the part of the deceased rider of the motorcycle as it is an admitted fact that the deceased rider of the motorcycle was not The Divisional Manager vs Smt. 5 having a valid and effective driving licence to ride the motorcycle.

sentences.text: Learned counsel would further submit that the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the deceased; while the deceased was proceeding on the motorcycle, the motorcycle skided and that is the reason for the accident, and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of the KSRTC bus.
Therefore, the learned counsel would pray for setting aside the liability saddled on the respondent- Corporation.

Thus, he prays for dismissal of the claimants'
- 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7821-DB appeal and for allowing the appeal filed by the- Corporation.

9. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, and on perusal of the appeal papers including the records of the Tribunal, the points that fall for consideration in this appeal are,
i) Whether the Tribunal is justified in saddling 75% and 25% liability on the driver of the bus and the deceased rider of the motorcycle respectively?
ii) Whether the income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.7,000/- per month is proper and correct?

iii) Whether the claimants are entitled for compensation under the heads 'future prospects'?
10.
The answer to above points would be in the affirmative, negative and affirmative respectively, for the following reasons.

(a) The accident that took place on 30.07.2015 involving motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-22/EN-0706 and KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-42/F-654 and the resultant death of Gadigeppa is not in dispute in this appeal.
The claimants are in appeal praying for enhancement of compensation, while the corporation is in appeal questioning the liability saddled on it.

(b) Learned counsel for the respondent-Corporation submitted that the deceased rider of the motorcycle had no valid and effective driving licence to ride the motorcycle as on the date of the accident, and that the accident took place solely due to negligent riding of the motorcycle by the deceased.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in Dinesh Kumar's case (supra) has made it clear that driving vehicle without licence itself would not warrant saddling of contributory negligence.

Further, it is observed that, the insurer has to establish the contributory negligence on the material - 12 - The Divisional Manager vs Smt. Jayashree W/O Fakirappa Jaragu on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183125908/
6 NC: 2024:KHC-D:7821-DB available on record.

entities.text: Divisional Manager vs Smt. Jayashree W/O Fakirappa Jaragu
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, in the instant case also, mere non-possessing of driving licence cannot be a reason to saddle contributory negligence on the deceased rider of the motorcycle.
But the material on record would indicate that the rider of the motorcycle i.e., the deceased also contributed to the occurrence of the accident.
The document Ex.P.3- spot mahazar would indicate that the accident has taken place at Desur on Belagavi-Khanapur road.
The accident in question is a head-on-collision.
P.W.1 has deposed that the deceased was proceeding towards Belagavi and bus was coming from opposite side i.e., from Belgaum.
The charge sheet was filed against the owner of the motorcycle and fine of Rs.1,000/- was imposed.
This clearly establishes that the rider of the motorcycle had also contributed to the occurrence of the accident.

Therefore,
the finding of the Tribunal, saddling contributory negligence to the extent of 75% and - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7821-DB 25% on the driver of the lorry and the deceased respectively is proper and correct.
(c) The claimants have stated that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by doing private service and Rs.10,000/- from milk vending business.
But, to establish the income and avocation of the deceased, no material whatsoever is placed on record.
In the absence of any material to establish the income, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the year 2015 is Rs.8,000/- per month which is fixed taking note of various factors including the minimum wages.
The notional income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.7,000/- per month is on the lower side.
Thus, the notional income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.8,000/- per month.

Admittedly, the deceased was aged 25 years and, in terms of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others2, the claimants would be entitled to adding 40% of the assessed income towards 'future prospects'.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the claimants are entitled to addition of 40% of the assessed income towards 'future prospects'.

The multiplier '18' adopted by the Tribunal taking into consideration the age of the deceased, and the deduction of 50% made by the Tribunal towards personal expenses of the deceased since he was a bachelor, are proper and correct.

(e) As the income of the deceased is assessed at Rs.8,000/-, the compensation, which the claimants would be entitled to, under the head 'loss of dependency' would be in a sum of Rs.12,09,600/-
[Rs.8,000/- + Rs.3,200/- (40%) = Rs.11,200/- less Rs.5,600 (50% of Rs.11,200/-) = Rs.5,600 x 12 x 18].
AIR 2017 SC 5157 - 15 - The Divisional Manager vs Smt. Jayashree W/O Fakirappa Jaragu on 12 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183125908/

In terms of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Nanu Ram and Others , the claimants, being the parents and sister of the deceased, would be entitled to a sum of Rs.40,000/- each on the head of 'loss of filial consortium'.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Further, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.15,000/- each under the heads 'loss of estate' and 'funeral expenses'.
11.

The modified compensation under various heads is as follows:
1) Loss of Dependency Rs. 12,09,600/-
2) Loss of filial consortium (to Rs. 1,20,000/-
claimants No.1 to 3) (Rs.40,000 x 3)
3) Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/-
 4) Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-
 TOTAL Rs. 13,59,600/-
Thus, the total modified compensation works out to Rs.13,59,600/-.

However, as the finding of the Tribunal with regard to contributory negligence is not interfered 2018 ACJ 2782 - 16 - NC: 2024:KHC-D:7821-DB with, the claimants would be entitled to only 75% of the above modified compensation i.e., Rs.10,19,700/- as against Rs.6,42,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

12. Hence, we pass the following:
ORDER a) M.F.A. No.103368/2017 filed by the claimants is allowed in part.
b) M.F.A. No.103089/2017 filed by the respondent-NWKRTC is dismissed.

c) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to the extent that the claimants are entitled to total compensation of Rs.10,19,700/- as against Rs.6,42,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
